methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $150M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $3.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Heirloom Carbon is a Series B climate and energy company founded by Shashank Samala and Noah McQueen that has raised $150M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws from a peer set of 3 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage private companies (KoBold Metals at $3.0B, Electric Hydrogen at $1.0B, and Amogy at $700M), supplemented by a broader comp universe of 8 private and 1 public company in the climate tech space.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $150M total raised as a proxy valuation base and applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement, implying $285M. Peer-median analysis across the three same-stage comparable companies yields a $1.0B midpoint, with observed valuations ranging from $700M to $3.0B. The latter method carries greater weight given Heirloom's alignment with these peers on sector and development stage.

Triangulating these methods produces a valuation range of $242M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $642M. The wide range reflects genuine uncertainty around stage-appropriate pricing within climate tech and the dispersion observed across near-peers. Key sensitivities include Heirloom's capital efficiency relative to KoBold and Electric Hydrogen, and whether the company's technology differentiation supports valuation toward the peer median or below.
